_comment: Verbatim HTML captured with curl from live pages. Not edited, not minified, not cherry-picked — including the ones the detector does badly on. Re-capture with widget/fixtures/refetch.sh.

fixtures.why: Shopify storefront, JSON-LD ProductGroup+Product+Offer, og:price:amount, cdn.shopify.com assets
Shopify in INR. JSON-LD is Organization-only, so the price has to come from og:price:amount="2,999" — comma grouping in a machine-readable field
The ticket case. JSON-LD MusicEvent + AggregateOffer + startDate + location. Also puts a street address in twitter:data1, which a naive meta reader would price.
Big retailer, clean JSON-LD Product+Offer, plus a BreadcrumbList and a 3DModel block to walk past
Next.js SPA. JSON-LD ProductGroup with hasVariant — the price lives one level down from the node that carries the name
Indian lakh grouping in the DOM (₹8,31,777) and a JSON-LD graph with Car/ProductGroup/AggregateOffer/FAQPage/BreadcrumbList all mixed together
MusicAlbum + albumRelease[].offers — the price is nested under a key most extractors do not recurse into
A search results page carrying 309 separate Product nodes and no indication which one the page is about. Tests that we pick one, say so, and drop the confidence for it.
No product markup at all. A real page with real 'Total Cost of Attendance' table rows — the DOM-total heuristic with nothing to lean on
Negative control. Prose full of dollar figures and the word 'total'. Must NOT return a confident total.
